domain: Dedicated search-only retrospective history; adaptively reused64-sequence search, not independent validation. Early contaminated pilot is not an uncontaminated experiment; supervisor feedback remains excluded.

records.hypothesis: Denser causal row sampling may capture short target changes missed by wider spacing; ridge regularization should control redundancy between neighboring rows.
With stride-5 sampling, the larger set of causal training rows may support a tenfold weaker ridge penalty, preserving useful residual coefficients and improving both targets' global WP.
Sampling every five rows may capture brief causal responses missed by the parent ridge's temporal sampling, improving both targets' global weighted Pearson without relying on another TCN.
Increasing the ridge penalty from 0.001 to 0.01 may suppress noisy coefficients from overlapping causal features and improve two-target global weighted Pearson on the fixed tuning set.
Increasing the ridge penalty from 0.01 to 0.1 may further reduce variance from correlated causal features, improving two-target global weighted Pearson on the fixed tuning set.
Adjacent causal rows may be redundant; increasing sample stride from 5 to 10 may reduce overrepresentation of slow periods and improve two-target tuning WP.
A causal TCN on the best regularized ridge pilot can learn temporal residual interactions that linear correction misses; clipped targets may stabilize its short training run.
A causal TCN trained on the best measured ridge system can learn short-lived nonlinear residuals that its regularized linear features miss; clipping may stabilize those residual targets.
Full-precision training may prevent the non-finite gradients seen with mixed precision while testing whether a causal TCN adds short-lived nonlinear corrections to the best measured ridge.
The rising training loss in the two-epoch TCN run suggests later updates may fit residual noise; one epoch may retain useful causal corrections and improve tuning WP.
Clipping may erase large residual corrections relevant to global WP; training the same one-epoch causal TCN on raw targets may improve on the pilot-best ridge base.
Clipping t0 as well as t1 may reduce the influence of rare large residuals and improve global WP; keep the best measured ridge training settings fixed to isolate this target-representation change.
Two epochs may let a causal TCN learn useful corrections for large residuals that clipped targets suppress; compare raw-target training with the best two-epoch clipped run.
Clipping t0 as well as t1 may reduce the influence of extreme residuals on the weaker target, improving mean global weighted Pearson under the regularization that worked best in prior pilots.
A two-epoch causal TCN on the best ridge pilot may capture short-range nonlinear sequence effects left in its residuals and raise combined global WP.
Clipped residual targets may reduce outlier-driven TCN updates, preserving the ridge pilot's t1 gain while improving the two-epoch causal correction.
The second TCN epoch may fit noisy clipped residuals: loss rose across update windows. One epoch may retain the causal correction and improve tuning WP.
Causal fast and slow state traces plus nonlinear random features may capture connectome response dynamics missed by static ridge and short residual TCNs.
